sources.title: A Nearly Quartic Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity
sources.retrieval_status: Official GitHub file page retrieved; raw endpoint returned unsupported application/octet-stream. Complete mathematical text read from the supplied extraction, with supplied PDF hash independently checked.
sources.read_scope: Entire extracted preprint, including Appendix A and references.
sources.remote_byte_identity: Not established. Packet version metadata is distinct from a fresh remote byte comparison.

sources.title: k-Forrelation Optimally Separates Quantum and Classical Query Complexity
sources.read_scope: First four PDF pages through HTML/PDF extraction; §3 proof outline and distribution statements; §5.4 main lower-bound proof; biased-Fourier identities (5.29)–(5.30).
sources.supports: The paper's fixed-k Forrelation lower-bound input and the earlier nearly cubic total separation.
sources.exact_lower_bound: For delta=2^(-5k), bounded-error randomized queries are Omega(k^(-29) (N/log(kN))^(1-1/k)).
sources.quantum_bound: Corollary 1.4 gives O(k 2^(10k)) queries for error 1/3.
sources.limits: The packet uses a weaker fixed-k asymptotic consequence with log^2 denominator. Its alternative formal proof is not this paper's proof. 'Only level k at a biased point' does not eliminate higher uniform Fourier levels.

sources.title: Degree vs. Approximate Degree and Quantum Implications of Huang's Sensitivity Theorem
sources.read_scope: First four PDF pages; proof of Theorem 2 assuming Theorem 3; §7 Conjecture 2.
locators: Proof of Theorem 2 assuming Theorem 3, printed p. 2
sources.supports: Universal D(f)=O(Q(f)^4), hence the randomized upper bound; the conjecture R(f)=O(Q(f)^3) refuted by the supplied construction.
sources.limits: Five-author paper. Do not confuse its numbering or attribution with four-author precursor arXiv:2004.13231.

sources.title: Separations in query complexity using cheat sheets
sources.read_scope: First four PDF pages; §§3.1–3.2, including the construction and Lemma 6 proof; §6.1 definitions inspected.
sources.supports: Earlier total-function separation of exponent 2.5; answer bits select a certificate cell, followed by verification. Provides direct prior art for address hiding and blank-array coupling.
sources.limits: The quartic construction adds outward-pointer disqualification and an arbitrary-comparison tournament. The 2016 theorem is not the quartic result.

sources.title: Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation
sources.read_scope: §2, invariant-subspace calculation, equation (8), Theorems 2–3 and QSearch description.
sources.supports: The successful component keeps its normalized direction under amplitude amplification. This supports the state-preservation ingredient.
sources.limits: Theorem 3 gives expected query cost and may run forever when success probability is zero. The required uniform cap comes from the supplied preprint's Lemma 3.1, not a direct restatement of BHMT Theorem 3.

sources.title: Improved Direct Product Theorems for Randomized Query Complexity
sources.supports: Per-instance capped direct-product bound under adaptive interleaving, based on continuation values and transcript-wise product laws.
sources.limits: An aggregate cap of rL cannot replace the separate cap of L on each of r instances. Independence of auxiliary information also matters. The attached Lean proof uses another finite-tree induction route.

sources.title: Fourier Growth of Parity Decision Trees
sources.read_scope: Abstract, §1.3 standard-decision-tree argument and Lemma 9 with proof/footnote 2; surrounding results.
sources.supports: The Azuma-along-the-tree, reverse-induction and union-bound method has prior art.
sources.limits: Publisher numbering is Lemma 9; the packet cites arXiv Lemma 1.9. This source does not independently establish that the packet's direct biased-measure adaptation is novel.
